attribution: Assistant analysis of retained decisions; no new student judgment or model execution

prior_decision.reason: This is the Cloudflare blog post announcing that the Deno team is joining Cloudflare to merge workerd and celld, enabling self-hosted Cloudflare Workers and Durable Objects. The student reviewer previously changed this item from defer to accept under v1, citing its potential effect on development infrastructure and distinguishing announced plans from verified capabilities. Under v2, that rationale holds and is reinforced: the post contains substantive technical content about the Workers programming model, the self-hosting gap (Durable Objects only work in single-instance mode in workerd), and an announced plan to merge celld into workerd. This is a vendor announcement from Cloudflare (source: Cloudflare blog, authored by Kenton Varda and Ryan Dahl), so all capabilities described — especially the merged self-hosting roadmap — must be treated as announced intentions, not verified outcomes. The post supports pieces 01 (what changed: Deno team joining Cloudflare, workerd/celld merge announced), 02 (scrutiny: the open-source escape hatch argument, lock-in claims vs. Cloudflare's rebuttal, admitted gap in Durable Objects self-hosting, no timeline given for merged production-ready tool), and 03 (implications: what the Workers programming model portability means for small teams considering platform commitment). Limitations: single vendor source, no independent corroboration, future delivery unverified, no commentary from developers who have tried self-hosting workerd in production.

claims_supported_after_introduction.statement: Cloudflare and Deno announce that the Deno team is joining Cloudflare and describe a plan to merge code and ideas from celld into workerd to improve self-hosting of the Workers programming model. The post says more announcements will follow in coming months and distinguishes that future work from the existing ability to self-host celld or workerd. It does not establish that the merged, supported experience has shipped or that a small team will find it economical.

The skills guidance, security announcement, production field guide, and hosting roadmap raise separate adoption questions: who evaluates code, what checks are affordable, who can stop automation, and where the application can run. Our recommendation is to begin with a bounded task whose result can be checked, then add autonomy only when those responsibilities are clear. Monitor the promised self-hosting work rather than planning a migration around an unshipped integration. This is a proposed decision process, not a measured cost or productivity result.

before: These claims lack the withheld evidence in the isolated baseline and must not be supported from it.
after: Introducing the eligible Deno source restores their evidence. Historical acceptance remains subject to the student policy: distinguish roadmap from shipped capabilities.
